title: Change 3D navigation region and link updates to an async process
body:
Changes 3D navigation region and link updates to an async process.

This was originally planned as a sibling PR to the navigation map async PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100497.

As visible by all the needed changes this turned out to be a far, far more complex endeavor so it did not make it for Godot 4.4.

## Dev / Review / Test Notes


Example project for testing

![test_project](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a160a72-ec76-4e96-a7d3-0963c1f70230)

[ClickToMoveTestMap.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20365158/ClickToMoveTestMap.zip)


<details>

<summary>Dev Notes</summary>

This is currently the 3D version only. As discussed with some devs the 2D version will be created when the 3D version is reviewed and settled. Just too much extra work to keep both versions updated throughout the entire process.

### Goals for this PR:
- Avoid performance issues caused my region internal navmesh updates by using threads.
E.g. if the navmesh was too big the sync on the region took too long and caused performance issues. In this case it did not help that the navigation map update was already done on a thread. The region update alone could cause the issue either due to a lack of slicing and partitioning of the user input navmesh or just too many regions updated all at once.
- Only update on regions and links what needs to be updated to avoid triggering unnecessary map updates.
Before on every map iteration build the map collected the geometry data from the regions in full. At this point that was the only way to move things out of harms way and still allow threaded pathfinding.

Especially with the partial updates this is still an ongoing process. I had to make the cut somewhere for this PR's scope. There are a lot of subtle issues with threads on improving this but also a lot of possible optimizations that could be done in a followup.

### How to test:
Use (or create) any 3D project that uses NavigationRegion3D / NavigationLink3D and change them at runtime.


<details>

<summary>Test script</summary>

Assuming a scene with NavigationRegion3D and NavigationLink3D nodes as direct children this script will print the changed iteration_ids when the navigation map changes.

``` gdscript
var old_map_iteration: int = 0
var old_region_iteration: int = 0
var test_iteration_data: Dictionary = {}

func _test_iterations():
	for region_node in get_children():
		if not region_node is NavigationRegion3D:
			continue
		
		var region_rid: RID = region_node.get_rid()
		var region_iteration_id: int = NavigationServer3D.region_get_iteration_id(region_rid)
		
		if not region_rid in test_iteration_data:
			test_iteration_data[region_rid] = region_iteration_id
		
		var old_region_iteration: int = test_iteration_data[region_rid]
		if old_region_iteration != region_iteration_id:
			test_iteration_data[region_rid] = region_iteration_id
			print("%s - region_iteration: %s" % [region_node.name, region_iteration_id])

	for link_node in get_children():
		if not link_node is NavigationLink3D:
			continue
		
		var link_rid: RID = link_node.get_rid()
		var link_iteration_id: int = NavigationServer3D.link_get_iteration_id(link_rid)
		
		if not link_rid in test_iteration_data:
			test_iteration_data[link_rid] = link_iteration_id
		
		var old_link_iteration: int = test_iteration_data[link_rid]
		if old_link_iteration != link_iteration_id:
			test_iteration_data[link_rid] = link_iteration_id
			print("%s - link_iteration: %s" % [link_node.name, link_iteration_id])

	if old_map_iteration != NavigationServer3D.map_get_iteration_id(get_world_3d().navigation_map):
		old_map_iteration = NavigationServer3D.map_get_iteration_id(get_world_3d().navigation_map)
		print("")
		print("map_iteration: %s" % NavigationServer3D.map_get_iteration_id(get_world_3d().navigation_map))
```
</details>

</details>

## How does it work?

This PR explained in one (animated) picture:

![navbuilder_async](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7aee2a69-8e24-45b5-ac12-2413caf7d3f7)

The navigation regions now by default update async using threads to improve performance and avoiding issues with main thread stalling when a region has a too big navmesh to process.

Navigation regions now cache a lot of their internals to reduce update overhead. The navigation map has far less work to do now on any map change as long as a lot of the regions do not change.

Due to the nature of async updates with threads this can cause additional delay on navmesh and navigation map changes.

For most projects this change will be barely noticeable but some projects might need to update parts of their logic or how they approach things. See the compatibility section below for details.

## Iteration changes

While the navigation map async change gave maps 2 iterations that ping-pong the async region update behaves different.

This is because it is entirely possible that two map iterations using pathfinding threads at the same time that operate on the same region iteration for an unknown amount of time ... while the region decides to change or switch maps ... .... while the connections on the regions .... while the navlinks ... while the workerpool .... .... why is there spaghetti lying all over the ground?

![spaghetti](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fd807b2-c760-4321-ad5d-fd741695b505)
_That Thing is back. Hide!_

Anyway ... let's summarize as things are complex.

In the async navigation map PR in order to make NavRegions and NavLinks asnyc workable with threads the new structs `NavRegionIteration` and `NavLinkIteration` were added.

These iteration update functions had to do full copies on every map iteration update. This was needed to keep things out of threads-harms-way. Doing full copies on every map update was obviously less than optimal for both performance and memory. This was always intended as quick  stop-gap solution to ship at least the async map update with Godot 4.4.

This PR now changes those region and link iteration structs to `RefCounted`. They are now only updated when really needed and shared among threads and map iteration builds while unchanged. As RefCounted they are also freed automatically when they are no longer used by the region/link and the map iterations and their pathfinding slots.

## Connection and Polygon changes

In order to achieve all these changes in this PR a lot of the connection and polygon storage had to be shuffled around to work with threads. Some stuff was moved away from the regions or polygons. E.g. the connections are no longer stored inside the polygons or NavRegion. They are now part of whatever iteration has build them, aka NavRegionIteration or NavMapIteration. When something was only viable for a map iteration it was also moved to the map, e.g. the NavLink polygons and connections. Also the polygon `Edge` struct was removed entirely and `Connection` is now its own struct.

![nav_mesh_edge_types](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/072e7534-5cfb-4165-8c68-a180cb08bbbc)

### Region internal connections

Regions now build all the internal navmesh polygon connections themself instead of the map. Those region internal connections are now cached on the region iteration. The connections are no longe recalculated on every map change as long as the region geometry remains unchanged (e.g. no transform or navmesh change).

The region iterations also keep a cache of their external edge keys that is used and processed by the map to merge navmeshes of different regions as before.

### Region external connections

The navigation map is responsible for the navmesh connections between region iterations along their outlines, aka their external edges.

For now those external connections are still recalculated on every map change. I had to make the cut somewhere for this PR's scope but it is a good target for further optimizations.

### Link connections and polygons

Navigation link polygons and their connections are moved to the map iteration. This is because links have a super awkward implementation where they create artifical new polygons to build the connection between actual navmesh polygons. Since those are only build by the navigation map they need to be part of the map iteration to persist through map changes and threading. The also can not randomly resize their arrays as it would invalidate all the navbase pointer magic.

## API changes

This PR adds new properties and api functions to push the region sync to an async process run on a background thread. The async update is enabled by default. If a project needs the old main thread sync back the async update can be disabled.

### ProjectSettings
New navigation regions use the ProjectSettings value from `navigation/world/region_use_async_iterations`.

### Server API
The async sync can be toggled for each region with the the NavigationServer API `region_set_use_async_iterations(region, enabled)` function.

```gdscript
void NavigationServer3D.region_set_use_async_iterations(region: RID, enabled: bool)
bool NavigationServer3D.region_get_use_async_iterations(region: RID)
```

### Where are the navlinks?
For navigation links there is no toggle. They are still synced on the main thread as their update cost is minimal. Their major performance cost happens on the navigation map build that is already run async.

## Compatibility

### Async updates
Navigation regions now update async with threads by default to improve performance.
Due to the nature of async updates this can cause additional delay on navmesh and navigation map changes.

For compatibility it is possible to turn back to a version of the older single-threaded mode that runs on the main thread.

The async update can be toggled in the ProjectSettings under `navigation/world/region_use_async_iterations`
The asnyc update can also be toggled per navigation region using the NavigationServer API `region_set_use_async_iterations()` function.

Note that for platforms without thread support the async feature is disabled automatically, no need to set it manually.

### Enabled property
Regions are now always a fixed part of the navigation map geometry no matter their `enabled` toggle. It is no longer possible to avoid navmesh overlap and merge conflicts by just disabling regions while still keeping them on the map.

The regions were always part of the map (and consumed processing on every update) but because some section of the map merge code did skip disabled regions it was not noticeable to users, there was no warning msg or error about it.

This change now "forces" the intended behavior of actually removing regions and their navmesh from a map that should not be a part of it.

### When sync? When update? When ready?
Due to the beauty of async and threaded processes going forward it becomes more important than ever to not expect a specific processing order / frame count until an update fully arrives, e.g. on the navigation map to affect a new path query.

Instead, use the `map_changed` signal to know when a map has changed, or poll the `map_get_iteration_id()`. If it is increased the map has finished building its newest iteration.

For the async region update there is no signal but the `region_get_iteration_id()` can be polled to know when a region iteration has finished.

**Note that just because a region iteration has finished does not mean that a map iteration has also finished that includes that region. Those are two different steps.**
